Chapter 2 Q1 — narrowing scope (no fringing)

Island-year spatial → within-lagoon → paired grids → (next) pooled / temperature

Author

Moorea Chapter 2 notes

Published

September 6, 2026

Analysis ladder (why the page is ordered this way)

Predictors that look clean island-wide can flip when we hold sampling composition more fixed. We narrow scope in steps:

  1. Island-wide × year (§1–4) — primary = spatial glmmTMB exponential + (1|Lagoon) (AICc vs Matérn/Gaussian).
  2. Within lagoon × year (§5.1) — same formula; spatial exp when residual Moran was high, else lm.
  3. Paired same grids (§5.2) — same rule on overlap sets.
  4. Pooled / temperature (§7) — not built yet; island-wide temp is mostly when surveyed.

Rule: any fit with residual Moran I > 0.05 & p < 0.05 was re-fit with spatial correlation before coefficients enter the primary tables (05t/05u).

1. What this is

Step 1 of the ladder: island-wide by year (spatial primary). Later sections hold lagoon and then grid composition more fixed when signs flip.

Question (Q1 snapshot): In each survey year, what predicts standardized algae cover across lagoon grids?

Choice Setting for this run
Grid 10 × 10 m
Years 2018–2024 (separate model each year)
Habitat Fringing dropped (Maharepa / Papetoai overrides applied first)
Lagoons Ch1 fishing filter ON — drop Tiahura & Papetoai; trim west Pihaena (lon < −149.850)
Spear NA → 0 (spear_na0)
Nutrient Required — static nutrient_allYear_percent_n_may (May %N IDW)
Photos ≥ 5 per grid-year
Model glmmTMB Gaussian + (1 \| Lagoon) + spatial
Spatial Exponential (exp) — AICc winner every year among exp / Matérn / Gaussian
Scaling Gelman 2-SD on continuous predictors
Primary response algae_std_A_CHS = A / (A + C + HS)
Secondary raw Algae_mean — still lagoon-only lmer (not spatialized)

Scripts: 05r (AICc kernel compare) → 05s (promote to primary). Lagoon-only lmer from 05c archived as sensitivity.
Outputs folder: models/10x10/baseline_by_year/ (primary) · …/lmer_lagoon_only_sensitivity/ (old lmer)

2. Model formula

For each year \(t\) (primary):

\[ \begin{aligned} \texttt{algae\_std\_A\_CHS}_t &\sim \texttt{coral\_std\_A\_CHS}_t + \texttt{herb\_biomass}_t \\ &\quad + \texttt{depth} + \texttt{maxRel} + \texttt{vrm} \\ &\quad + \texttt{offshore\_ratio} + \texttt{min\_dist\_to\_pass} + \texttt{perc\_MPA} \\ &\quad + \texttt{nutrient\_allYear} + \texttt{spearDensity} \\ &\quad + (1 \mid \texttt{Lagoon}) + \texttt{exp}(\texttt{pos3} + 0 \mid \texttt{group}) \end{aligned} \]

  • pos3 = numFactor(centroidLon, centroidLat); one island-wide spatial group.
  • Kernel chosen per year by AICc among converging exp / Matérn / Gaussian (Gaussian never started; Matérn usually failed Hessian/σ² checks; exp won all years).
  • Static geography / MPA / nutrient / spear do not carry a year suffix.
  • Herb and coral are same-year as the algae response.
  • All listed predictors are required: complete.cases drops any grid missing depth, coral, herb, nutrient, spear, etc.

Why spatial? Lagoon-only lmer left strong residual Moran I every year (neighbors too similar). Exponential spatial absorbs that map structure so fixed-effect SEs are not anti-conservative.

Why lagoon RE still? Some lagoons have more algae than others for unmeasured lagoon-level reasons; (1|Lagoon) absorbs that baseline in addition to fine-scale spatial correlation.

Depth coding (easy to misread)

depth_m_mean is bathymetry in meters where negative = below the surface (more negative = deeper).
A positive depth coefficient therefore means shallower grids → more algae (not “deeper → more algae”).

4.3 Hypothesis scorecard — island-wide spatial primary

Island-wide spatial std models only (7 years). Within-lagoon / paired scorecards come later in §5 once composition is held fixed.

Coral (matched scale)
Competition for space
More living coral → less hard-substrate space for algae (same-year coral matched to algae).

Shallower grids favor algae mainly via more light; related shallow-water processes (warming, nearshore runoff, access) may contribute but are partly shared with other predictors.

More structure → algae (relief caveat)

dirs mixed but majority matched 		Weak / unstable; structure pathway only weakly supported.
VRM (rugosity)
More complex terrain → algae
Higher VRM = more fine-scale terrain complexity (not organism density).
Expected + via more microhabitat / short-dispersal retention and/or reduced grazing access on complex surfaces.
Caveats: complexity can also shelter herbivores (→ more grazing → less algae), and often correlates with coral framework (partly absorbed by the coral term).
+ sig 3/7
+7 / −0 		✓ all + mixed 3/7
★ all match hyp (3) 		✓ dir matches
(★ 3/7) 		Supports complexity → algae (herbivore / coral caveats).
Offshore ratio (shore→crest)
Shore→crest position (no signed hyp)
Offshore ratio indexes shore→crest position (higher = closer to crest).
Crestward grids are typically shallower, more wave-exposed, and more continuous reef; shoreward mid-lagoon (no fringing) is slightly deeper, calmer, with sparser bommies.
Shallow/light and structure pathways would push algae up crestward, but those are largely absorbed by depth / maxRel / VRM / coral.
The residual offshore effect is mainly exposure / zoning, which can help or hurt algal cover depending on assemblage — so Exp. ?; treat as context, not a signed driver.
? sig 2/7
+3 / −4 		✗ flips mixed 2/7 no signed hyp Residual exposure / zoning — context, not a signed driver.
Distance to pass
Closer to pass → more flow → less algae
Distance to pass (min_dist_to_pass_m): higher = farther from a pass.
Near passes: stronger exchange / flushing, often cooler or less stagnant water, and commonly sandier channel / pass-mouth habitat.
Farther from passes: more interior lagoon water (longer residence time), calmer retention, and typically more continuous mid-lagoon reef.
Signed hyp follows the flow / flush pathway: nearer → less algae, so Exp. + (farther → more algae).
Caveats: passes can also deliver nutrients / propagules (→ opposite sign), and near-pass habitat/structure is partly absorbed by depth / maxRel / VRM / coral.
+ sig 1/7
+3 / −4 		✗ flips mixed 1/7
★ all opposite (1) 		✗ lone ★ opposite Flow / flush story not supported (delivery / habitat caveats).
% MPA
Protection → less algae
Higher % MPA = more of the grid under protection.
Inside / high-MPA: reduced fishing pressure → expected herbivore recovery → less algae.
Outside / low-MPA: open to fishing → fewer herbivores → more algae.
Note: same causal path as spear and herb — with those in the model, residual MPA is hard to identify; also MPA siting is non-random (habitat differences can look like protection effects).
- sig 0/7
+3 / −4 		✗ flips never ★ no ★ years Residual protection after herb / spear not identifiable.
Nutrient (%N May)
Bottom-up nutrients
Higher nutrient supply (static May %N IDW) → more algae (bottom-up).
High %N: more enriched water / watershed–nearshore influence as mapped → expected faster algal growth.
Low %N: more oligotrophic / flushed conditions → less algae.
Caveats: this is a static spatial proxy (one May %N IDW field reused every year — not year- or survey-matched in situ N). It also tracks geography (esp. distance to pass), so β is residual enrichment after other terms.
+ sig 2/7
+6 / −1 		✗ flips mixed 2/7
★ all match hyp (2) 		~ all 2 ★ match;
dirs mixed but majority matched 		Bottom-up direction plausible; limited by static May proxy.
Spear density
More fishing → more algae
Higher spear density → fewer herbivores → more algae (fishing pathway).
High spear: more fishing pressure → expected herbivore depletion → more algae.
Low / zero spear: little mapped effort → expected more grazing → less algae.
Caveats: same causal path as herb and MPA — with those in the model, residual spear is hard to identify as an independent effect. NA→0 coding mixes true zeros with unobserved effort. Spear is a Ch1 spatial layer (not year-matched to each survey).
+ sig 0/7

5. Narrower scope — lagoon, then same grids

Steps 2–3 of the ladder. Island-wide mixes which lagoons appear each year, and within a lagoon the surveyed cells turn over. After coral (−) and depth (+) hold under spatial island-year models, we ask: do other predictors stay signed when we stop mixing lagoons, then when we hold the same cells?

Step Held fixed Model (current) High residual Moran
2. Within lagoon × year One lagoon Spatial exp if Moran high; else lm 30/31 spatialized (§5.3)
3. Paired grids Same grid_IDs in both years Same rule on overlap 12/16 spatialized (§5.3)

5.2 Paired grids (same cells, two years)

What this is: same formula, but only on grids surveyed (and complete-case) in both years of a pair (overlap n ≥ 50). Strictest check that year-to-year flips aren’t just surveying different parts of the lagoon.

48 lagoon×year-pairs have enough overlap to fit (across 7 lagoons). Most other combinations lack resurveyed grids (n < 50) — turnover is a real design limit.

Stability across those pairs (one row per predictor):

One “pair” = one lagoon + two years fit on the same overlapping grids. For each pair we get two coefficients (year A and year B). Same sign in year A & B counts how many of the 48 pairs keep the same sign across those two years (ignoring whether either is ★). Both ★ + same sign is stricter: among pairs where both years are ★, how many still match sign.
